In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah al-'Adiyat

It is Meccan.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By the racers, panting﴾. 'Ali and Ibn Mas'ud said: they are the camels.

'Ali said: On the day of Badr there were only two horses: one belonging to al-Miqdad, and the other to al-Zubayr.

Ibn 'Abbas said: they are the horses.

This opinion is more evident.

He swears by the horses that run in the way of Allah, and by their panting (dabh).

Dabh is the sound of their bellies (ajwaf). It is also said: it is the sound of their breaths when they run.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is neither neighing (sahil) nor snorting (hamhama).

And His saying: ﴿By those that strike sparks, striking [them]﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: they are the camels, which strike sparks with their soft pads (manasim). But according to the saying of Ibn 'Abbas: they are the horses, which strike the stones with their hooves, so that fire is produced.

And His saying: ﴿So those that attack at dawn﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: they are the camels, when they pour out from Muzdalifah (Jam'). According to the saying of Ibn 'Abbas: they are the horses that raid in the way of Allah. Qatadah said: they made a raid when the morning came.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 100, verse 4:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then raise thereby clouds of dust﴾. According to the saying of Ibn Mas'ud, "they raise [the dust] in the valley," so the pronoun refers to something not mentioned explicitly. According to the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, [the pronoun refers] to the place of the raid (al-mughar).

Mujahid related from Ibn 'Abbas: al-naq' is dust (al-turab). Qatadah said: it is the fine dust (al-ghubar).

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So they penetrate thereby into the midst of a gathering﴾. According to the view of Ibn Mas'ud, it means the gathering at Muzdalifah; and according to the view of Ibn 'Abbas, it means the gathering of the enemy. So Allah, Exalted is He, swore by the Lord of these things. It was also said: He swore by these very things themselves. It was further said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had dispatched a expedition (sariyyah) to the Banu Kinanah, and they raided at dawn and penetrated into the midst of the enemy's gathering, and they were horsemen; so Allah, Exalted is He, swore by them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 100, verse 6:

His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord﴾. Upon this the oath was sworn.

His saying: ﴿ungrateful﴾ meaning: disbelieving (kafur). It was said: it is the miser of bad character.

In some reports traced back to the Prophet, transmitted through Abu Umamah from the Prophet regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord﴾, he said: "It is the one who eats alone, withholds his gift, and beats his servant."

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This hadith was related to us by the judge Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qantari; we were told by Muhammad ibn al-Husayn [al-Haddadi]; we were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya; we were told by Ishaq ibn Ibrahim; we were told by (al-Mu'tamin) ibn Sulayman, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, the hadith.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed he is, to that, a witness﴾, meaning: and indeed Allah is a witness to that, that is, to his disbelief.

Ata related from Ibn Abbas, who said:

And His saying: ﴿And indeed he is, in love of wealth, intensely tenacious﴾. Its meaning: indeed, man, because of his love of wealth, is stingy.

It is said: "shadid" (intense) and "mushaddid" mean: stingy (bakhil).

Tarafa said:

(I see death selecting the noble and choosing the choicest property of the niggardly, the tight-fisted)

That is: the stingy (bakhil).

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered forth﴾. That is: taken out. Ibn Mas'ud recited "bahatha" (searched out), and it is reported from others, namely Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he recited "bahthara" (overturned), that is: turned upside down.

Allah's words: ﴿And that which is in the breasts is brought out﴾ mean: that which is in them is made manifest.

It is also said: it means He gathers together what is in the breasts, that is, what is in the pages of deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 100, verse 11:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully Acquainted with them﴾ means: He is Knowing (ʿalim). It is also said: it means He will recompense them for their deeds. Similar to this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾, meaning: Allah will recompense them for what is in their hearts.

Likewise is His saying: ﴿And whatever good you do, Allah knows it﴾, meaning: He will recompense for it. It was also said regarding His saying: ﴿and what is within the breasts is made known﴾, meaning: He will distinguish what is in them of good and evil. And Allah knows best.
